expectations.text: Cites the information supplement Security Considerations for AI Systems published in September 2026
expectations.evidence: In September 2026 the PCI Council published an information supplement titled 'Security Considerations for AI Systems'.

expectations.text: Explains information supplements are guidance and do not create new requirements
expectations.evidence: It is an information supplement, so it is guidance and not a new PCI DSS requirement... Information supplements are not part of the standard. You are not assessed against them as requirements.

expectations.text: Notes Secure SLC v2.0 (September 28, 2026) also addresses AI and digital tools in lifecycle processes
expectations.evidence: Secure SLC Standard v2.0 (September 28, 2026) adds coverage of digital tools and AI in vendor lifecycle processes.

expectations.text: Confirms PCI DSS v4.0.1 itself is unchanged by the supplement
expectations.evidence: no new AI-specific control was added to PCI DSS v4.0.1. v4.0.1 remains the current version... It does not change your PCI DSS validation obligations.

expectations.text: Gives practical application advice for AI touching cardholder data environments
expectations.evidence: Requirement-by-requirement table (scope, PAN/SAD in prompts, TPSP, MFA, logging) plus six practical steps including an AI tool inventory and acceptable use rule.
